full_text_en:
Xingtai City People's Procuratorate v. Lu Guoping — homicide case

[Ruling Summary]

The defendant's conduct has constituted the crime of intentional homicide, with serious consequences, and should be punished according to law. However, in view of the fact that this case arose from a civil dispute, both parties bore some fault in the cause of the incident, and the defendant intervened to prevent another person from committing suicide while in custody, the death penalty imposed on him need not be executed immediately.

Criminal Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2004) Xing Fu Zi No. 160

Defendant Lu Guoping, male, born on August 2, 1979, Han ethnicity, from Shahe City, Hebei Province, educated to junior high school level, farmer, residing in Gaodian Village, Shahe City. Arrested on April 17, 2000. Currently in custody.

The Intermediate People's Court of Xingtai City, Hebei Province, having tried the case of Xingtai City People's Procuratorate charging the defendant Lu Guoping with the crime of intentional homicide, rendered a criminal附带 civil judgment on June 22, 2002, as (2002) Xing Xing Chu Zi No. 54, finding the defendant Lu Guoping guilty of intentional homicide, sentencing him to death, with a two-year suspension of execution, deprivation of political rights for life, and ordering joint compensation with Lu Liguo (co-defendant in the same case, already sentenced) to the plaintiff in the附带 civil action for economic losses of RMB 8,000. After the judgment was announced, the plaintiff in the附带 civil action appealed, and the Xingtai City People's Procuratorate lodged a protest. The High People's Court of Hebei Province, on December 11, 2002, rendered a criminal附带 civil judgment as (2002) Ji Xing Yi Zhong Zi No. 766, setting aside the sentencing portion of the first-instance criminal附带 civil judgment against the defendant Lu Guoping, finding Lu Guoping guilty of intentional homicide, sentencing him to death, deprivation of political rights for life, and reported the case to this Court for approval according to law. On May 13, 2003, this Court rendered a criminal ruling as (2003) Xing Fu Zi No. 19, setting aside the criminal附带 civil judgment of the High People's Court of Hebei Province (2002) Ji Xing Yi Zhong Zi No. 766, and remanding the case to the High People's Court of Hebei Province for retrial. After retrial, the High People's Court of Hebei Province, on March 24, 2004, rendered a criminal附带 civil judgment as (2003) Ji Xing Yi Zhong Zi No. 704, setting aside the criminal附带 civil judgment of the Intermediate People's Court of Xingtai City (2002) Xing Xing Chu Zi No. 54, finding the defendant Lu Guoping guilty of intentional homicide, sentencing him to death, deprivation of political rights for life, and again reported the case to this Court for approval according to law. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and conducted a review of this case. The review is now concluded.

After review, it is confirmed that: At approximately 8:00 p.m. on March 18, 2000, the defendant Lu Guoping, after drinking alcohol, drove a motorcycle carrying Lu Liguo (co-defendant in the same case, already sentenced) to return home. When they arrived west of Gaodian Village, Shahe City, they encountered the victim Cui Shulin, who had fallen to the ground after drinking alcohol while driving a motorcycle, blocking the road and affecting vehicle passage. Lu Guoping told Cui Shulin to move out of the way, but Cui did not move. An argument and then a fight ensued. Lu Guoping and Lu Liguo knocked Cui Shulin to the ground. While Lu Liguo held down Cui Shulin and beat him, Lu Guoping struck Cui's head with a stone. Thereafter, Lu Guoping and Lu Liguo fled the scene. Cui Shulin died on the spot due to a subdural hematoma caused by blunt force to the head.

The above facts are confirmed by the scene investigation record, the extracted stone used as the weapon, the forensic examination conclusion, and witness testimony. The defendant also confessed. It is sufficiently established.

The Court holds that the defendant Lu Guoping's conduct has constituted the crime of intentional homicide, with serious consequences, and should be punished according to law. The convictions in the first and second instance judgments are accurate. However, the finding in the first and second instance judgments that the defendant Lu Guoping drove the motorcycle over the victim Cui Shulin's leg, thereby triggering the argument and fight between the parties, is supported only by the testimony of witness Xi Haisheng, without corroboration from other witness testimony or the defendant's confession, and is inconsistent with the public security organ's autopsy report; the evidence is not solid or sufficient, and this Court does not find this fact. In view of the fact that this case arose from a civil dispute, both parties bore some fault in the cause of the incident, and the defendant Lu Guoping intervened to prevent another person from committing suicide while in custody and other specific circumstances, the death penalty imposed on the defendant Lu Guoping need not be executed immediately. Pursuant to Article 199 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Item (3) of Article 285 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 232 and Paragraph 1 of Article 57 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The sentencing portion of the criminal附带 civil judgment of the High People's Court of Hebei Province (2003) Ji Xing Yi Zhong Zi No. 704 against the defendant Lu Guoping is set aside;

2. The defendant Lu Guoping is found guilty of intentional homicide, sentenced to death, with a two-year suspension of execution, and deprivation of political rights for life.

This judgment shall become legally effective upon service.

Presiding Judge: Li Wuqing

Judge: Zhang Simin

Judge: Zhu Weide

July 21, 2004

Clerk: Liu Shiqian

[Introduction to the Presiding Judge]
Li Wuqing, senior judge: born in 1951, with a college diploma in law. Appointed Deputy Chief Judge of the Second Criminal Division of the Supreme People's Court in 1992, and Deputy Chief Judge of the First Criminal Division of the Supreme People's Court from 2000.
